Hi Jonas,

Thanks for taking this—FinTrust is onboarding Redwood as a supplier and our Risk team has a short list of items we need to complete the vendor risk assessment. Could you please provide the following by EOD Wednesday (Pacific):

1) Current Recovery Time Objectives (RTO) and Recovery Point Objectives (RPO) for the following service tiers: control plane (API & auth), inference (real-time text generation), and persistent stores (model artifacts & user embeddings). If numbers vary by region/tier, include both primary and fallback values.

2) Evidence of the most recent disaster recovery / failover test: date, scope (partial vs full failover), runbook followed, and test outcome.

3) A redacted copy of the backup/retention policy for customer data and the retention timeline for artifacts needed to restore embeddings/models.

4) Any documented RTO measurement logs (timestamped) or dashboards you can share (CSV export is fine).

We treat this as confidential. If you prefer to send via a secure Drive link or a signed NDA channel, let me know.

Appreciate it—we're aiming to close the assessment before contract signature.

Best,
Samantha Lee

Subject: Re: FinTrust BCP/DR evidence request: RTO/RPO and recent drills

Samantha —

Thanks for the clear list. I've pulled together the requested materials and attached a short, redacted package to this thread: a one-page BCP summary, the aggregated RTO/RPO CSV export, the most recent failover test report (2025-06-30), and our backup retention policy. Key highlights up-front:

- Control plane (API/auth): RTO = 2 minutes (automated failover within region), RPO = 0s for metadata/auth tokens (replicated synchronously), 5 minutes for analytics/event windows.
- Inference (real-time generation): RTO = 20s for hot path (if warmed), 2 minutes cold start for model loading across GPU pools; RPO = near-zero for request-state (we do not persist session KV unless configured by customer).
- Persistent stores (model artifacts, embeddings): RTO = 3 hours for full rebuild from backups in a regional outage, RPO = 4 hours for snapshots (daily snapshots plus incremental every 4 hours for customer artifact store).

A few notes about the numbers: the inference "hot path" number assumes KV cache priming and that model artifacts have been pre-pulled. In cross-region full failover scenarios we fall back to a compatible quantized variant of the model to meet latency SLOs.

Attachments included: redwood_bcp-summary-2025-07.pdf, rto-rpo-dashboard-agg-2025-06.csv, failover-test-2025-06-30.pdf, backup-retention-policy-2024-11.pdf.

If you want, we can provide a short walkthrough of the failover test artifacts and logs — happy to schedule a 30m call with our Platform Reliability owner (Karthik) and Security lead (Laura).

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales Lead
Redwood Inference

Samantha —

Per your follow-ups, please find the requested clarifications and the CSV extract below (redacted IDs):

1) Inference hot-path measurement (US-West, 2025-06-30 drill):
CSV extract rows (UTC):
2025-06-30T14:02:13Z,failover_start,us-west-2-inference-pool
2025-06-30T14:02:33Z,endpoint_cutover,us-west-2-proxy
2025-06-30T14:02:34Z,first_successful_serve,request_id=redacted

The 20s figure reported is the median time-to-first-successful-serve across 50 warm requests; p95 in that drill was 48s due to two cold-starts on large model variants. The attached CSV (rto-rpo-dashboard-agg-2025-06.csv) includes the full drill exports.

2) Persistent store "3-hour rebuild" definition: this is scoped to restoring artifacts and embeddings to an alternate region from snapshot + incremental logs, including a quantization step when the primary artifact is a higher-precision variant. Typical steps:
- snapshot copy initiated to target region (automated)
- artifact unpack and integrity check (automated)
- model quantization and validation (automated, but requires spot GPU allocation)
- artifact rollout to inference pools and cache warm-up (automated; cache warm-up can be manual for very large corpora)
Estimated median time: 2h45m; conservative SLA-aligned RTO = 3h. Manual intervention is limited to approval of GPU allocation in extreme capacity-constrained events (we have automated quota increase playbooks).

3) Integrated test coverage: We executed an end-to-end integrated failover on 2025-03-18 (control plane + inference + storage) scoped to a simulated region outage. Outcome: successful automated failover with <5% request error spike during cutover window; detailed report is attached (failover-test-2025-06-30.pdf includes component and integrated test appendices).

Next steps: if you'd like an interactive review we'll set up a 30-minute technical call with Karthik and Laura — available Thu 07/17 10–11am PT or Fri 07/18 1–3pm PT.

Let me know which slot works and I'll send a calendar invite plus the secure Drive link.
